name: Moraceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: For the local Morus/Maclura pool, combine woody habit, milky latex, stipules, tiny unisexual flowers and multiple fruits; then split mulberry from Osage-orange by infructescence shape.

project_scope.selection_mode: Central Texas family-first module across Morus and Maclura
project_scope.note: The four source taxa include native/local Morus and Maclura anchors plus introduced Morus alba as a comparison; species nativity remains a separate lane.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: On a local woody plant, check for milky latex and stipules, then look for tiny unisexual flowers packed into heads/spikes and a multiple fruit made from an entire inflorescence rather than one ovary.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Local genera are deciduous trees or shrubs with alternate simple leaves and stipules. Leaves may be entire, toothed or lobed. Milky latex is a strong local clue.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers are tiny and unisexual, with a reduced sepaloid perianth and no showy corolla. Flowers are crowded into heads or spikes; local fruiting structures become obvious multiple fruits.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Individual one-seeded fruits are combined with fleshy perianth/receptacle tissue into a syncarp/multiple fruit—elongate in Morus and large globose in Maclura.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Woody + milky latex + tiny unisexual flower clusters + a whole-inflorescence fruit is the local Moraceae package.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: woody habit + latex → stipule/node → tiny unisexual inflorescence → multiple fruit → Morus-vs-Maclura → Rosales comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Mulberries and Osage-orange look nothing alike at fruiting size, but they share the same family trick: lots of tiny flowers packed together, later forming one multiple fruit.

steps.title: 1 · Confirm the woody latex clue
steps.photo_role: fresh twig/leaf petiole showing white latex
steps.look_for: Milky sap from a freshly damaged local Morus or Maclura twig/leaf.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates the local family quickly from Celtis and Ulmus lookalikes.

steps.title: 2 · Find the stipule scar at the node
steps.look_for: Alternate leaf with a stipule or stipule scar associated with the bud/node.
steps.why_it_matters: Adds a structural clue that is safer than leaf shape alone.

steps.title: 3 · Shrink your attention to the flowers
steps.look_for: Tiny greenish unisexual flowers crowded into spikes or heads instead of one showy flower.
steps.why_it_matters: Explains how the later multiple fruit is assembled.

steps.title: 4 · Read the fruit as an inflorescence
steps.photo_role: fruit close-up + diagram of many flower units
steps.look_for: Many one-seeded flower units fused/crowded into a single fleshy multiple fruit.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the family confirmation that separates a mulberry or Osage-orange from a simple berry or drupe.

steps.title: 5 · Morus door: elongated mulberry syncarp
steps.look_for: Toothed or lobed leaf and an elongated berry-like multiple fruit built from a cylindrical pistillate inflorescence.
steps.why_it_matters: Covers Texas mulberry, red mulberry and introduced white mulberry in one genus-level architecture.

steps.title: 6 · Maclura door: giant globose syncarp
steps.look_for: Woody thorny tree architecture and a large globose, wrinkled multiple fruit.
steps.why_it_matters: The fruit is unmistakable, but tying it back to family structure makes the lesson transferable.

comparisons.title: Moraceae vs Urticaceae
comparisons.rule: Both have tiny often unisexual flowers and can share stipule/cystolith traits. Local Moraceae is woody, strongly latex-bearing and makes multiple fruits; local Urticaceae is herbaceous and ends in individual achenes.

comparisons.title: Moraceae vs Cannabaceae
comparisons.rule: Celtis is woody and Rosales-adjacent but makes individual fleshy drupes and lacks the local Moraceae latex + multiple-fruit package.

comparisons.title: Moraceae vs Ulmaceae
comparisons.rule: Ulmus makes dry samaras; local Moraceae makes fleshy multiple fruits assembled from many flowers.

visual_lesson.caveat: Moraceae is globally diverse and latex/fruit architecture vary. For this project, the Morus/Maclura combination is intentionally local rather than a universal key to every fig-family genus.

genera.fast_cue: toothed/lobed leaves + cylindrical flower clusters → elongated mulberry multiple fruit
woody thorny tree + very large globose wrinkled multiple fruit

teaching_cautions: Morus alba is an introduced comparison in the source pool; do not let its abundance turn it into a native anchor.
Do not call a mulberry or Osage-orange fruit a single berry; it is a multiple fruit assembled from many flowers.
Do not use leaf lobing by itself to separate Morus species.
